1

 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 10-09-2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 10-09-2023 at about 6.20 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing No. KA-44-S-8099 as a pillion rider and her son was riding the motor cycle and when they reached in front of Honnavalli Mahanavami Mantapa, Honnavalli, at that time the rider of another motor cycle bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042 has ridden the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Tiptur Govt. Hospital,
wherein she took treatment as inpatient.

Later she was shifted to Hassan Govt.
Hospital and underwent MIPPO WITH PTCLP and got discharged.

The petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards surgery, medical expenses, conveyance,
nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, working as agriculturist and also doing milk vending business and thereby earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner has suffered disability and lost her earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.1 - owner has not appeared before the court, hence placed as Exparte.

Respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting issuance of policy to the motor cycle bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042 and its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and the rider of the said vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exaggerated and baseless.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing No. KA.44-Y-9042 by its rider, in RTA took place on 10.09.2023 at about 6.20 p.m. in front of Honnavalli Ma- Suvarnamma vs Gangadhara on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137667284/
2 hanavami Mantapa, Honnavalli- Huli- halli road, Tiptur Taluk, Tumkuru Dis- trict 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?

3 . What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.
Further, Dr. Chidanand K J C wase examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.14 & 15.

On the other hand the official of 2nd respondent insurance company is examined as RW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to R3 and RTO, Hassan examined as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R4.
6.
Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed her affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of her case, she has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, seizer mahazar, IMV reports, wound certificate and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 9.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR which is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the relative of the petitioner.
The contents of Ex.P1 & 2 is in consonance with the contents of petition regarding the rash and negligent driving by the rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P4 rough sketch was prepared by the I.O.

On perusal of the contents of mahazar and rough sketch the petitioner was proceeding in straight road in the left side of the road and at same time, rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042 dashed against the motor cycle in which the petitioner was proceeding.
The Ex.P3 & 4 spot mahazar along with sketch shows that the accident spot is in the left side portion of the road.
This shows that the offending motor cycle bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042 has came in the left side of the road and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.
The Ex.P6 & P7 are the IMV reports wherein the motor cycle in which the petitioner was proceeding has got damages in its front left side and the offending vehicle also got damages in its front side.

This shows that the rider Suvarnamma vs Gangadhara on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137667284/
3 of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042 came to its wrong side and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.

The contents of mahazar and rough sketch along with IMV report helped the petitioner to prove the alleged negligence of motor cycle bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042.
10.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 1 day in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly, instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought and the offending vehicle is implicated in the case even though it is not involved in the accident.
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioner doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.

11. No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 10-09-2023 at about 6.20 p.m. but the FIR was lodged on 11-09-2023 at about 2.45 p.m. and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after one day of occurrence of the accident.

But the informant in the Ex.P2 first information it is stated that soon after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Tiptur Government hospital and thereafter shifted to Hassan Government hospital and underwent with treatment and also as there was no one to look after the petitioner, they were unable to give the complaint immediately.

Further the Ex.P8 is the wound certificate also depicts that on 10-09-2023 at about 7.40 p.m. the petitioner was taken to Tiptur Government hospital for treatment with history of RTA between two bikes near Honnavalli Huliyar road at 6.30 p.m.
The contents of wound certificate helped the petitioner to prove the alleged accident and also it shows that the delay of 1 day is backed with genuine reasons.

Hence the delay of one day, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint, Ex.P8 wound certificate and Ex.P11 discharge summary it cannot be considered as inordinate.

12. Further on perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 & 4 spot mahazar along with sketch and Ex.P6 & 7 IMV reports, the petitioner succesfully established the negligence of rider of motor cycle bearing No.
KA-44-Y-9042 and thereby no reasons are made out to consider the contributory negligence by the petitioner as the petitioner is a pillion rider and the accident is in the left side portion of the road.
13. Ex.P9 charge sheet is filed against the rider of the motor cycle bearing KA-44-Y-9042, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of rider of the motor cycle bearing KA-44-Y-9042.
No other grounds are made out by the respondents to show the contributory negligence from the petitioner.
14. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
But the RW.1 is not an eye witness and who is deposed on the basis of documentary evidence where the criminal records shows the negligence of rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the rider of offending motor cycle bearing KA-44-Y-9042.
15.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 for the offences punishable under Sec.279 & 338 of IPC.

At this juncture, I would like to quote the following judgment wherein it states that;
Suvarnamma vs Gangadhara on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137667284/
4 2009 ACJ 287 ( National Ins. Co. V/s.
Pushparama and others), wherein it is held that, Certified copy of the criminal court records such as FIR, recovery and mechanical inspection of the vehicle or documents are of sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the rider was negligent.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

16. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

18. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by their negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.

19. The contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 rough sketch and Ex.P6 & 7 IMV reports falsifies the contention of respondent no.2 about the contributory negligence of petitioner for the occurrence of accident.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 8 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
20. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 10-09-2023 which is caused by the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 which belongs to respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.2.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
21.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that she has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the vehicle of respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.

Suvarnamma vs Gangadhara on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137667284/
5
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 49 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P10 shows the date of birth of the petitioner as 01.01.1973, the accident was occurred on 10-09-2023, as on the date of accident petitioner was aged about 50 years.

In the petition itself she has averred that immediately after the accident she was shifted to Tiptur Govt. Hospital and later shifted to Hassan Govt. Hospital, wherein she took treatment as inpatient.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P11 the petitioner was inpatient from 11-09-2023 to 12-09-2023 and sustained type 2 both bone fracture proximal 1/3rd right leg with open fracture of base of 2 nd metatarsal of left foot.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.80,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P12, amounting to Rs.2,370/-.
The medical bills are not seriously disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.2,400/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period: The petitioner has stated that she was working as agriculturist and also doing milk vending business and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
In this regard petitioner has not produced any documents.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2023.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.11 the petitioner was admitted to Chamarajendra HIMS Teaching Hospital, Hassan and later shifted to Hassan Govt. Hospital wherein she was admitted as inpatient for a period of 02 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total four months period including 2 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4 months = Rs.64,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by her the petitioner examined Dr.Chidanand K J C, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics hospital as PW.2 and through him clinical notes and X-ray were got marked at Ex.P14 & 15.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained type 2 open both bone fracture proximal 1/3rd right leg and fracture 2 nd metatarsal left foot and she underwent treatment in the form of CRIF with MIPPO plate and screws.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered disability for limb at 50% and whole body disability at 16.33%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.

Suvarnamma vs Gangadhara on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137667284/
6
According to the petitioner she was working as agriculturist and also doing milk vending business.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P11 the petitioner was inpatient from 11-09-2023 to 12-09-2023 and sustained type 2 both bone fracture proximal 1/3rd right leg with open fracture of base of 2 nd metatarsal of left foot.
The fractures in the leg certainly causes disability to the petitioner and it may affect on her occupation of agriculturist to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 14% to the whole body.
The petitioner has produced her Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P10, as per these documents the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 01-01-1973.
The accident was occurred in the year - 2023.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 50 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '13'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 13 X 14% =Rs.3,49,440/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P11 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 02 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P8 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are simple and grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period she spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained she is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained simple and grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 02 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.2,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 02 days in the hospital.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospitals for the injuries sustained by her, which might certainly have deprived her of the basic comforts and enjoyment.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P11 the petitioner was inpatient from 11-09-2023 to 12-09-2023 and sustained type 2 both bone fracture proximal 1/3rd right leg with open fracture of base of 2nd metatarsal of left foot.
The fracture is at leg and foot.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 in his affidavit evidence has stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.25,000/-.
Hence, by looking to the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the treatment taken by her, I inclined to award Rs.20,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

7 a.
Towards pain and agony Rs. 80,000/- b.

Towards medical expenses Rs. 2,400/- c.

laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs.3,49,400/- e.

Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 30,000/-
conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 2,000/- g.
Towards loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/- h.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 20,000/-
Liability:- According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the motor cycle bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.

23. The respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 3 and also examined RTO, Hassan as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R4.
24.

In the written statement of the respondent No.2- insurance company admitted the issuance of insurance to the offending motor cycle bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042,
but in view of the specific contention of the respondent No.2 insurance company that respondent No.1 being the owner of the said vehicle has violated the policy conditions, as the respondent No.1 has handed over the offending Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 which is insured with respondent No.2 to the rider who did not possess a valid and subsisting driving license to ride the offending Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042.
25.

Precisely, it is the specific case of the respondent No.2 insurance company that the rider of the offending Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042, did not possessed a valid driving license and hence was not competent to ride the offending vehicle Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042, and secondly the respondent No.1 with full knowledge has allowed unauthorized person to ride the offending Motor Bike bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042, which is in gross violation of the insurance policy.
26.

In respect of this, on perusal of Ex.P9 head of charge sheet, the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 and 338 of IPC and Sec. 181 of IMV Act is invoked against one Gangadhara who was the rider of the Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 at the time of accident.
The IO in his investigation has also found that the said Gangadhara who was the rider of Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 at the time of accident was not having valid DL at the time of accident.
The IO has issued notice to the respondent No.1 as per Ex.R2 to furnish the driving licence details of the rider of Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 at the time of accident as per Ex.R2.

To the said Suvarnamma vs Gangadhara on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137667284/
8 Ex.

sentences.text: R2 , the respondent No.1 has given reply as per Ex.R3 wherein he himself admitted that himself was the rider of Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 at the time of accident and he has no driving licence at that time.
In spite of service of summons, the respondent No.1- owner has neither appeared nor adduced any evidence to prove the contrary to Ex.R3- reply or to the Ex.P9- charge sheet.

27. Further the official of RTO is also examined as RW.2 wherein RW.2 filed endorsement as per Ex.R4 by reporting that they have not found any driving license details of Gangadhara S/o Venkatabhovi in their records and also in their online computerized Sarathi-4 Technology.
The official of Respondent no.2 insurance company examined as RW.1 in support of their defence.

By the evidence of Rw.1 in corroboration with contents of Ex.P9 charge sheet and Ex.R3 reply given by the respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 insurance company successfully discharged its burden that the rider of Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 was not having valid DL at the time of accident and thereby the condition of the policy is violated.

28. The respondent No.2 insurance company successfully discharged the burden and proved the violation of conditions of policy as the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 was not having valid DL at the time of accident.
Hence, next point needs to be considered is to whom the liability has to be fastened.

29. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 insurance company argued that the evidence of the RW.1 as well as RW.2 clearly set out the aspect regarding the rider of Suzuki Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 was not having valid driving licence at the time of accident and the respondent No.1 being the owner with full knowledge handed over the insured vehicle to the rider to ride the same without driving licence hence, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
30.
By keeping the arguments canvassed by both the parties in background, there is no dispute that at the time of accident the Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 was covered with insurance.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established.

As per Ex.R1 policy it contains the condition that it covers the risk provided the person driving the vehicle holds an effective and valid driving licence at the time of accident and is not disqualified from holding such licence.

31. In this case, the respondent No.1 owner of the Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 even after the service of summons has not lead any evidence to show that he has not violated the policy condition willfully.

Thereby the conduct of respondent No.1 -owner allowing the unauthorised person to ride the Suzuki Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 is a fundamental breach of policy condition and thereby the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
The respondent No.1 being the owner cannot take the benefit of his own wrong.

Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of policy conditions and liability to pay compensation is on the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence, the respondent No.1 owner is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
The amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses shall not carries any interest as it is awarded for future medical expenses.

Suvarnamma vs Gangadhara on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137667284/
9
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
32.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,97,840/- (Rupees Five lakhs ninety seven thousand eight hundred and forty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses), from the date of petition till the realization from respondent No.1.
The petition against the respondent No.2 - insurance company stands dismissed.
The respondent No.1 - owner is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 10-09-2023.
2.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner has suffered disability and lost her earning capacity.
Respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting issuance of policy to the motor cycle bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042 and its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and the rider of the said vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing No. KA.44-Y-9042 by its rider, in RTA took place on 10.09.2023 at about 6.20 p.m. in front of Honnavalli Ma- Suvarnamma vs Gangadhara on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137667284/
2 hanavami Mantapa, Honnavalli- Huli- halli road, Tiptur Taluk, Tumkuru Dis- trict 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?

opennyai_summary.arguments: The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 1 day in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly, instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought and the offending vehicle is implicated in the case even though it is not involved in the accident.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioner doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 for the offences punishable under Sec.279 & 338 of IPC.
Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.
16. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 8 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
20. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 10-09-2023 which is caused by the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 which belongs to respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.2.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained she is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
Precisely, it is the specific case of the respondent No.2 insurance company that the rider of the offending Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042, did not possessed a valid driving license and hence was not competent to ride the offending vehicle Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042, and secondly the respondent No.1 with full knowledge has allowed unauthorized person to ride the offending Motor Bike bearing No. KA-44-Y-9042, which is in gross violation of the insurance policy.
26.
In respect of this, on perusal of Ex.P9 head of charge sheet, the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 and 338 of IPC and Sec. 181 of IMV Act is invoked against one Gangadhara who was the rider of the Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 at the time of accident.
By the evidence of Rw.1 in corroboration with contents of Ex.P9 charge sheet and Ex.R3 reply given by the respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 insurance company successfully discharged its burden that the rider of Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 was not having valid DL at the time of accident and thereby the condition of the policy is violated.
28. The respondent No.2 insurance company successfully discharged the burden and proved the violation of conditions of policy as the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 was not having valid DL at the time of accident.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established.
As per Ex.R1 policy it contains the condition that it covers the risk provided the person driving the vehicle holds an effective and valid driving licence at the time of accident and is not disqualified from holding such licence.
31. In this case, the respondent No.1 owner of the Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 even after the service of summons has not lead any evidence to show that he has not violated the policy condition willfully.
Thereby the conduct of respondent No.1 -owner allowing the unauthorised person to ride the Suzuki Motor Bike bearing No.KA-44-Y-9042 is a fundamental breach of policy condition and thereby the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
The respondent No.1 being the owner cannot take the benefit of his own wrong.
Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of policy conditions and liability to pay compensation is on the respondent No.1 owner.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

Hence, the respondent No.1 owner is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,97,840/- (Rupees Five lakhs ninety seven thousand eight hundred and forty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses), from the date of petition till the realization from respondent No.1.
The petition against the respondent No.2 - insurance company stands dismissed.
The respondent No.1 - owner is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
